I have a project that depends on mathlib (constructed using the blueprint template) and while everything works smoothly (thanks everyone who put effort into making it very userfriendly), lake does not download mathlib:

└─$ lake update
info: toolchain not updated; already up-to-date
info: mathlib: running post-update hooks
Current branch: HEAD
Using cache (Azure) from origin: leanprover-community/mathlib4
Attempting to download 6759 file(s) from leanprover-community/mathlib4 cache
Downloaded: 0 file(s) [attempted 6759/6759 = 100%, 0 KB/s]
Warning: some files were not found in the cache.
This usually means that your local checkout of mathlib4 has diverged from upstream.
If you push your commits to a branch of the mathlib4 repository, CI will build the oleans and they will be available later.
Alternatively, if you already have pushed your commits to a branch, this may mean the CI build has failed part-way through building.
Already decompressed 1306 file(s)

I can see any reason why this is the case - git reports that the HEAD commit of mathlib is the right one, git diff in .lake/packages/mathlib does not find anything weird. Is there some dependency hell?
It seems like this should work
Is your project public?
https://github.com/mcdoll/DynamicalSystems
I have docs in FLT but don't have docgen explicitly listed in my lakefile, no idea if this has anything to do with it though
Yeah, you've got a setup where the lakefile for the docs is generated on the fly
To my surprise, I can reproduce

doc-gen main depends on a different version of plausible than mathlib master. If you remove doc-gen from your lakefile for now and update, you'll get the mathlib version and the cache works.

CC @Kim Morrison
Perfect, it seems to work now

The problem is that lake exe cache computes content hashes using LEAN_SRC_PATH as set by Lake for the downstream project. When the downstream project pins different versions of shared dependencies than mathlib does, the cache binary resolves module source files to the wrong versions.

In this case, the DynamicalSystems project has different versions of plausible and Cli pinned in its lake-manifest.json compared to what mathlib's lake-manifest.json specifies:

plausible: downstream b3dd6c3ebc0a vs mathlib 2b93f2523263
Cli:       downstream 474983579ecc vs mathlib 0c688ceba0d3

Just get rid of these from your lakefile, and allow them to come transitively from Mathlib.
Yeah, not helpful
#36173 should give actionable messages about this situation in future.
I would guess that leanblueprint new did the bad update - the template looks fine

Ruben Van de Velde said:

Yeah, not helpful

Ah, you mean because it didn't understand that those dependencies came via doc-gen, rather than directly?
Yeah
Is there some better actionable message that cache can give in this case? I tried #36173, but I agree it is a bit misleading here.

The real answer is actually "put Mathlib first" (or maybe last? someone would have to check) in the require statements, so it wins regarding versions of upstream deps. (And, don't put those upstream deps explicitly in the lakefile.)
Right, but there's no redundant deps in the lakefile here

Wasn't the problem here that Moritz had both doc-gen and mathlib in the lakefile, and mathlib should have been last, which would have (undocumentedly but apparently true?) let it "win" what went in the lake-manifest?

So the advice on #36173 should include putting Mathlib last?
I had delegated the PR before realising that this thread pointed out some further issues.

Damiano Testa said:

I had delegated the PR before realising that this thread pointed out some further issues.

No problem, you can undo, or I just won't merge until we've worked out the correct advice here.

Kim Morrison said:

Wasn't the problem here that Moritz had both doc-gen and mathlib in the lakefile, and mathlib should have been last, which would have (undocumentedly but apparently true?) let it "win" what went in the lake-manifest?

So the advice on #36173 should include putting Mathlib last?

My point is that you can remove doc-gen, but then you don't have doc-gen, so it's not as easy as "why are you importing batteries manually when it's also a transitive dependency". That said, putting mathlib last (if that guarantees it takes precedence) is a reasonable workaround, but also doesn't guarantee that the version of plausible from mathlib works with doc-gen. Anyway, that's a wider versioning discussion that I don't really want to have right now (or at all) :)

That versioning problem will actually be solved quite soon: doc-gen and mathlib will be able to depend on different versions of plausible! Mac has some treats for us in upcoming versions. So we just need "good enough" solutions in the meantime.
I've pushed some changes, with a better message (and use Lake tools to analyze the manifests properly).

So I tried update and followed the new message to move mathlib to the last in lakefile.toml. It seems to have correctly downloaded all caches, butt when I build the project, it still rebuilds the entire Mathlib...
toolchain:4.29.0-rc4
mathlib commit: 8a9bdec
Oh, apparently it didn't rebuild the entire Mathlib. It finished around after 2000 files. Not sure why this happened
What project is this about, @Weiyi Wang ? Do you depend on doc gen?
It is my personal project that depends on both mathlib and doc gen. I tried it again on another project of mine and observed that it needed to rebuild some part of mathlib and took about 5 minutes
When I get time I can try a clean reproduction and report more details
Is mathlib last in your Lakefile?
There's also #36367
Yes

Ruben Van de Velde said:

There's also #36367

if this is the only issue, it should be resolved by lake exe cache unpack/unpack! (or ofc, bumping mathlib to include the fix)
